title: 432 Park Avenue
visualBrief: Detailed exposed-concrete Manhattan tower with physically punched10ft windows, recessed aluminum hopper units, five genuine open double-storey drum levels and the separately mapped lower L-shaped podium.

sourceFacts.reviewScope: Complete static medium-fi exterior of the 425.5m square concrete tower and its mapped adjacent L-shaped lower podium, including all five authored double-row open mechanical bands and cylindrical cores, 56th Street arrival and roof. The unchanged 292,272-triangle detailed source master is reproducible. Four separate browser recipes preserve all principal masses and open levels. District uses the reusable 256px window_punched graph at an explicit six-column, 90-geometrical-row motif phase; its generic opening ratio and pane color approximate the building, and graph tiling is not a metric window survey. Street restores every authored square pane and closeup restores intrados, simplified perimeter/hopper frames and core ribs. Centimeter joints, handles, hardware, measured core drums, terrace furnishing, interior fit-out and live tenant signage are outside browser detail. Ninety geometric rows and marketing floor numbers are distinct. Standalone Park Avenue retail cube and neighboring older buildings are independent site structures outside this tower/podium asset and remain eligible for ordinary map rendering; replacement is disabled. No downloaded mesh or copied facade photo is redistributed. Three mapped arrays were freshly confirmed unchanged, and the southwest entry fixes signed orientation. Absolute site elevation, street grade and physical phone/laptop timings remain unmeasured.
sourceFacts.browserFacadeMotif: Canonical window_punched, six repeats across each 28.5m side, one repeat per 4.7244m geometrical row; generic pane ratio is an accepted district approximation.
sourceFacts.browserErrorScope: Skyline omits planter details up to1.05m and averages closed facade color; district keeps all five genuinely open bands but uses a shared approximate window motif. Street omits0.9m terrace guards within its1m whole-asset bound. Closeup keeps guards and replaces centimeter boxed frames with planar strips;0.15m allows omitted podium frame depth and microscopic hardware. The street and closeup recipes now include continuous physical window intrados, and podium frame strips sit3cm proud of glazing to prevent depth flicker. Corner piers keep their full clipped half-width.

reconstruction.frame: White concrete exterior with90 geometrical grid rows; five open pairs at rows20/21,34/35,48/49,62/63 and76/77 are reconstructed from the architect elevation and completed facade photographs. Marketing floor numbers are not physical row indices.
reconstruction.windows: Individual10ft panes recessed4in, physical concrete intrados, aluminum perimeter frames and reconstructed inset hopper sash. Exposed drum floors include continuous cylindrical mechanical enclosures and full-height open exterior grid.
reconstruction.base: Independent offset tower way463593207 retained inside mapped30m podium463386820. Southwest arrival matches mapped main entrance and architect56th Street description. Separate distant retail cube excluded.

geographicProposal.notes: Fresh OSM API snapshot on 2026-10-10 confirms exact Q233940 main outline 261499924, separate 30m podium 463386820, offset shaft 463593207 and main entrance 5995346749. All three footprint arrays equal the preserved source evidence. Native +X points 28.550deg east of north toward 57th Street, +Z points southeast toward Park Avenue. The mapped main entrance lies on native -X, agreeing with the architect 56th Street arrival and resolving the 180deg ambiguity. The published 28.5m shaft is not enlarged to the whole podium. Retained anchor and heading use a rigid pose, no scale change. Accepted map registration tolerance is 2m and 1 degree. Ground Y0 is the main entry datum; absolute elevation and street grade are supplied by the host and are unmeasured. Footprint replacement is disabled so separately mapped neighboring/site buildings remain available.
